The Wheat and the Tares
TAIRZ
noun phrase
From the Greek zizanion, the darnel weed that mimics wheat until the ear appears; the parable of the field sown with good seed and tares.

📖 Biblical Definition

The parable of the Wheat and the Tares teaches the mingling of the good and the evil in the world until the harvest at the end of the age. The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field; but while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way (Mat 13:24-25). When the blade sprang up, the tares appeared also; and the servants would have gathered them at once, but the householder forbade them, Let both grow together until the harvest, lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them (Mat 13:30). The LORD Himself expounded it: He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man; the field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one; the enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels (Mat 13:37-39). The dictionary marks this parable as the great word on patience and judgment. The field is the world, not the church only, and in it the righteous and the wicked grow side by side, not to be severed by the hand of man. So the Scripture teaches that the separation belongs to God, and is reserved to the last day, when the Son of man shall send forth His angels, and they shall gather out of His kingdom all things that offend, and cast them into a furnace of fire; then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun (Mat 13:41-43).

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The parable in which wheat and tares grow together in the field of the world until the angels sever them at the harvest of judgment.

expand to see more

THE WHEAT AND THE TARES, the parable of the field sown with good seed and with tares.

The good seed is the children of the kingdom; the tares are the children of the wicked one.

The field is the world, where the righteous and the wicked grow together.

The householder forbids the servants to root up the tares before the harvest.

At the end of the world the angels sever the wicked from the just for judgment.

📖 Key Scripture

Mat 13:30 — "Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn."

Mat 13:38 — "The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one;"

Mat 13:39 — "The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels."

Mat 13:43 — "Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A parable of the kingdom teaching the patient mingling of good and evil until the final judgment; it has drawn little redefinition.

expand to see more

The parable of the Wheat and the Tares has drawn little redefinition from the present age, surviving as the LORD’s own teaching on the field of the world and the harvest at the end. The dictionary records it that the reader may mark the patience of God in the present mingling and the certainty of the severing to come.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the separation of the righteous and the wicked belongs to God and is reserved to the last day. The field is the world, where wheat and tares grow together; the servants are not to root up the tares before the harvest, for that judgment is the angels’ work at the end of the age. So the Scripture forbids both a careless tolerance that denies any harvest and a hasty zeal that would sever now what God reserves to Himself; and it sets before the children of the kingdom the day when they shall shine forth as the sun, and the wicked be cast into the furnace of fire.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Greek zizanion, the darnel weed, the parable names the wheat and tares grown together until the harvest.

expand to see more

The Wheat and the Tares — from the Greek zizanion, the darnel weed.

The good seed is the children of the kingdom, sown by the Son of man.

The tares are the children of the wicked one, sown by the devil.

The field is the world, where both grow together until the harvest.

The reapers are the angels who sever the wicked from the just at the end of the world.

Usage

"Like the wheat and the tares, the righteous and the wicked grow together in the field of the world until the harvest."

"Let both grow together until the harvest, for the severing is the angels’ work at the end of the age."

"Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father."
